newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa posts minor losses, seen eroding.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa posts minor losses, seen eroding.

text.p: London cocoa futures ended Friday's session with minor losses after trading in a range for most of the day.
Traders said a feeling of inertia had surrounded the futures again after a brief correction from the lows seen earlier this week. Some said prices looked set to erode again to revive buying interest.

"We will to have to either move down to a new low area or move above 950 (basis March) to see what sort of selling there is. All the business that can be done at this price level has been done," said one trader.
"The last couple of days has been a non-event," he said.
Friday's session saw a meagre turnover of 3,044 lots featuring a light volume of belated hedging and industry price fixing.
At the close, the benchmark March contract posted a loss of two stg at 934 stg -- a session low -- after trading in a four-stg range. December also shed two to 902.
Traders said the physical market remained in a state of havoc after sterling's wild fluctuations against the French franc and the dollar.
Traders noted Ghana's second week of purchases totalling 23,010 tonnes, with a cumulative of 55,140 by October 24 compared with a cumulative 65,587 on October 26, 1995.
But a safer crop arrival picture would emerge at the end of November, they said.
The structure was broadly unchanged with Dec/March stuck at 33-34 stg.
Technical support is along a downtrend channel in place since the middle of October at around 930-925 stg.
